title: An image analysis protocol using CellProfiler for automated quantification of post-ischemic cardiac parameters
protocol: Download the VCCRI GitHub Cardiac-Image-Analysis repository.
Click the green “Code” button on the main page.
Download the zip folder and move the uncompressed directory to the desired location.
Open Fiji and run macro #1 (1_Macro_pipeline1.ijm) on image folder 1 (1_Images_pipeline1_WGA_IB4).
Select “Plugins > Macro > Run…” in Fiji.
Select macro #1 in the first popup window, click Open.
Select the desired input folder, and in the second popup window, click Open.
Wait until the log states the conversion is complete or processing updates have stopped before moving to the next step.
Open Fiji and run macro #2 (2_Macro_pipeline2.ijm) on image folder 2 (2_Images_pipeline2_WGA_CD45).
Select “Plugins > Macro > Run…” in Fiji.
Select macro #2 in the first popup window, click Open.
Select the desired input folder, and in the second popup window, click Open.
Wait until the log states the conversion is complete or processing updates have stopped before moving to the next step.
Run macro #3 in Fiji on image folder 3.
Select “Plugins > Macro > Run…” and open macro #3.
Select the desired input folder for macro #3 execution.
Wait until processing updates stop before moving to the next step.
Run macro #4 in Fiji on image folder 4.
Select “Plugins > Macro > Run…” and open macro #4.
Select the desired input folder for macro #4 execution.
Wait until processing updates stop before moving to the next step.
Mix 15 mM sterile HCl with human recombinant leptin.
Change the number of “workers” in CellProfiler to 16 to increase parallel processing.
Open CellProfiler and select “Menu > Preferences > Maximum Number of workers: 16”, then click OK.
Load the required CellProfiler pipeline by dragging and dropping Pipeline #1 - 1_Capillary_per_CM_segment.cpproj into the left-hand box below the setup tabs.
Import image files using the Images module.
Establish rules to group images in the NamesAndTypes module.
Change output directory settings in the View output settings box.
Add modules to the pipeline via the Addition box.
Test pipeline and segmentation settings by pressing Start Test Mode button.
Run final pipeline analysis by clicking Analyze Images button.
Identify primary objects module for nuclei segmentation.
Use advanced segmentation settings by checking Yes.
Set size threshold parameters to remove objects smaller and larger than specified diameter limits.
Configure intensity thresholding method and settings for segmentation.
Select methods for dividing segmented objects.
Click step button to progress between modules in test mode.
Open pre-processed image files in CellProfiler.
Sort images by dragging and dropping them into the appropriate tabs.
Select the “NamesAndTypes” tab in CellProfiler.
Drag and drop image files or entire folders into the software.
Arrange files by selecting rules that apply to the image names.
Duplicate another image channel as needed.
Click "Update" to ensure filenames are correctly aligned.
Change output directory settings to desired file location.
Select "Start Test Mode".
Identify the "Identify Primary Objects" module.
Check "Use advanced settings" Yes.
Identify the input image as DAPI or another appropriate name based on naming convention.
Set “Object diameter in pixels” to low minimum and high maximum values, e.g., Sizes = 15 and 60 pixels respectively.
Set “Lower and upper bounds on threshold” between flexible values, e.g., 0.001–1.0.
Set “Threshold correction factor” to a flexible value, e.g., 0.8.
Set “Threshold smoothing scale” to 1.3488 (Sigma of 1.0).
Set “Suppress Local maxima distance” and “Size of smoothing filter” to lower than the minimum object size, e.g., 10 for both.
Set "Method to distinguish clumped objects" and "Method to draw dividing lines between clumped objects" to Shape.
Click “Step” to observe segmentation quality in the popup window with defined settings.
If the settings are not appropriate, consult Table 2 for troubleshooting options.
Once the segmentation is accurate, click “Step” for both “Overlay Objects” and “Display Data on image” to check segmentation and label objects.
Click “Step” on the “Save Images” module to save segmented images as numbered overlays.
Test segmentation settings on 10–20 images in test mode before running finalized analysis.
Ensure segmentation settings work for many images and not just a small subset.
Adjust the number of workers to match the physical cores (CPUs) available in the computer.
Do not exceed 4 or 8 workers if using a machine with low RAM (4/8 GB) and only 8 CPUs.
Be aware that processing time may be several hours for more than 1000 images depending on pipeline complexity.
Close other programs before running segmentation tests to avoid popup windows from CellProfiler.
Uncheck “eye” symbols in pipelines to speed up the processing.
Use the CellProfiler help button (Question Mark box) to access detailed information and settings guidance.
Click “Step” to observe segmentation quality in the popup window with defined settings.
If these settings are not appropriate, consult Table 2 and the CellProfiler Question Mark box for troubleshooting.
Once the segmentation is accurate, click “Step” for both “Overlay Objects” and “Display Data on image”, to check segmentation and label objects for downstream analysis quality control.
Finally, click “Step” on the “Save Images” module to save segmented images as numbered overlays.
Select “Expand or Shrink Objects” to expand masked objects arbitrarily by a specified number of 5 pixels, click “Step”.
Select “Convert Objects to Image” to provide an image to mask blank space, click “Step”.
Select “Mask Image” to generate the blank space mask, click “Step”.
Generate a ‘seed’ region which is inside the WGA boundary using the next “Identify Primary Objects” module with Adaptive, Otsu, Two class threshold.
Set “Object diameter in pixels” to relatively flexible low minimum and high maximum values (e.g., Sizes = 30–50 and 150–250 pixels, respectively).
Set “Lower and upper bounds on threshold” between relatively stringent values (e.g., 0.5–0.97), with a stringent (1.0) “Threshold correction factor”.
Set “Threshold smoothing scale” to 1.3488 (Sigma of 1.0).
Set “Suppress Local maxima distance” and “Size of smoothing filter” to lower than the minimum object size (e.g., 25–30 for both).
Set “Method to distinguish clumped objects” and “Method to draw dividing lines between clumped objects” to Intensity and Shape, respectively.
Click “Step” to observe segmentation quality in the popup window with defined settings.
Select the “Identify Secondary Objects” module.
Expand segmentation outwards from the ‘seed’ region using Adaptive, Otsu, Gradient Watershed method.
Set “Lower and upper bounds on threshold” between 0.2–1.0.
Set “Threshold correction factor” to 1.0.
Set “Threshold smoothing scale” to 1.3488 (Sigma of 1.0).
Click “Step” to observe segmentation quality in the popup window with defined settings.
Subtract objects segmented in 14b from 14a using the “Identify Tertiary Objects” module.
Select “Overlay Objects” and click “Step” for quality control.
Select “Display Data on image” and click “Step” for label object quality control.
Select the "Measure Object Size Shape" module to quantify geometric parameters of segmented capillaries and cardiomyocytes.
Click “Step”.
Select the "Measure Image Area Occupied" module to quantify geometric parameters of segmented capillaries and cardiomyocytes.
Click “Step”.
Select the "Calculate Math" module to quantify the ratio of capillaries to cardiomyocytes.
Click “Step”.
Use the "Display Density Plot" module to show the shared distribution of capillary and cardiomyocyte areas.
Click “Step”.
Select the "Display Histogram" module to show the distribution of cardiomyocyte areas.
Click “Step”.
Click “Step” on the "Save Images" module to save segmented images as numbered overlays.
Load the required CellProfiler pipeline.
Drag and drop the pipeline (Pipeline #2 - 2_CD45_per_CM_segment.cpproj) into the left-hand box below the setup tabs.
Alternatively, build pipelines to suit individual channel layout and experimental setup by selecting modules based on logic outlined in relevant documentation.
Open pre-processed image files in CellProfiler.
Select the “Images” tab.
Drag and drop image files or entire folders into CellProfiler.
Select the “NamesAndTypes” tab.
Arrange files by selecting rules that apply to the image names.
Add another image channel by selecting Duplicate this image.
Click “Update”, ensuring file names are correctly aligned.
Select “View output settings” to change the output directory.
Enter “Start Test Mode”.
Progress through the nuclei segmentation steps from the first “Identify Primary Objects” module.
Proceed forward with CD45+ cell segmentation after running the first “Save Images” module.
Select “Smooth” module to homogenize the appearance of CD45+ cells.
Use the function Smooth keeping edges and automatically calculate the Artifact diameter.
Keep the Edge Intensity difference at 0.1.
Click “Step”.
Load the required CellProfiler pipeline by dragging and dropping Pipeline #3 - 3_EdU_FB_segment.cpproj into the left-hand box below the setup tabs in CellProfiler.
Open pre-processed image files in CellProfiler and sort them.
Select the “Images” tab and drag and drop image files or entire folders into CellProfiler.
Select the “NamesAndTypes” tab.
Arrange files by selecting the rules that apply to the image names.
Add another image channel by selecting Duplicate this image.
Click “Update”, ensuring that the filenames are correctly aligned.
Select “View output settings” to change the output directory to desired file location.
Enter “Start Test Mode”.
Proceed forward with CF TdT+ cell segmentation.
Select the “Identify Primary Objects” module.
Segment using Adaptive, Otsu, Three class threshold.
Set “Object diameter in pixels” to 30 and 120 pixels for minimum and maximum values respectively.
Set “Lower and upper bounds on threshold” between flexible values (e.g., 0.05–1.0).
Set “Threshold correction factor” to 0.75.
Set “Threshold smoothing scale” to 1.3488 (Sigma of 1.0).
Assign pixels in the middle intensity class to Background.
Set “Suppress Local maxima distance” and “Size of smoothing filter” to higher than the minimum object size, e.g., 40 for both.
Set “Method to distinguish clumped objects” to Intensity.
Set “Method to draw dividing lines between clumped objects” to Shape.
Click “Step” to observe segmentation quality in the popup window with defined settings.
Once the segmentation is accurate, click “Step” for both “Overlay Objects” and “Display Data on image” modules.
Check segmentation and label objects for downstream analysis quality control.
Select the “Identify Primary Objects” module in CellProfiler for EdU+ nuclei segmentation.
Set an Adaptive, Otsu, Two class threshold for object segmentation.
Set "Object diameter in pixels" to low minimum and high maximum values (e.g., Sizes = 15 and 60–80 pixels).
Set “Lower and upper bounds on threshold” between flexible values (e.g., 0.001–1.0) with a Threshold correction factor of 0.8.
Set “Threshold smoothing scale” to 1.3488 (Sigma of 1.0).
Set “Suppress Local maxima distance” and “Size of smoothing filter” to lower than the minimum object size (e.g., 10 for both).
Set “Method to distinguish clumped objects” and “Method to draw dividing lines between clumped objects” to Shape.
Click “Step” to observe segmentation quality in the popup window with defined settings.
Once accurate, click “Step” and perform both “Overlay Objects” and “Display Data on image” for quality control.
Select the “Measure colocalization” module.
Select EdU and CF images for comparison.
Set the threshold at 10% of the maximum intensity across the entire image.
Check Yes for “Run all metrics” option.
Quantify overlapping segmented CFs with segmented EdU+ nuclei.
Relate objects by selecting the “Relate Objects” module.
Designate segmented CFs as “Parent objects” and segmented EdU+ nuclei as “Child objects”.
Save the children with parents as a new object set (check Yes).
Select “Convert objects to image” to save the related EdU+ CFs (double positive) objects as a new Colour image.
Click “Step” for both “Overlay Objects” and “Display Data on image” to check segmentation and label objects for downstream analysis quality control.
Quantify parameters relevant to amounts of double positivity and CF sizes.
Select the “Measure Object Size Shape” module in CellProfiler.
Click “Step” after selecting the module.
Select the “Measure Image Area Occupied” module.
Click “Step” after selecting the module.
Select the “Calculate Math” module.
Click “Step” after selecting the module to quantify the percentage of proliferating CFs and output results to an "Image" .csv file.
Click “Step” on the “Save Images” module to save segmented images as numbered overlays.
Analyze images once all segmentation steps are optimized by selecting “Analyse Images” in CellProfiler.
Run the pipeline to generate data and segmentation images in .csv and .tiff formats, respectively, for downstream processing.
Proceed forward with TUNEL+ cell segmentation after running the first “Save Images” module.
Select the “Identify Primary Objects” module for segmenting TUNEL+ nuclei.
Set “Object diameter in pixels” to relatively stringent low minimum and high maximum values (e.g., Sizes = 15 and 60–80 pixels, respectively).
Set “Lower and upper bounds on threshold” between flexible values (e.g., 0.001–1.0), with a flexible (0.8) “Threshold correction factor”.
Set “Threshold smoothing scale” to 1.3488 (Sigma of 1.0).
Set “Suppress Local maxima distance” and “Size of smoothing filter” to lower than the minimum object size (e.g., 10 for both).
Set “Method to distinguish clumped objects” and “Method to draw dividing lines between clumped objects” to Shape and Shape, respectively.
Click “Step” to observe segmentation quality in the popup window with defined settings.
If these settings are not appropriate, consult Table 2 and the CellProfiler Question Mark box for troubleshooting.
Once the segmentation is accurate, click “Step” for both “Overlay Objects” and “Display Data on image” to check segmentation and label objects for downstream analysis quality control.
Click “Step” on the “Save Images” module to save segmented images as numbered overlays.
Select the “Relate Objects” module with segmented nuclei as the “Parent objects” and TUNEL+ nuclei as the “Child objects”.
Click “Step” to relate objects.
Save the children with parents as a new object set by checking Yes.
Convert related TUNEL+ DAPI+ (double positive) objects to image and save it as a new Colour image.
Click “Step” for both “Overlay Objects” and “Display Data on image” to check segmentation quality control.
Once all segmentation steps are optimized, select “Analyse Images” to run the pipeline.
